chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Never invited downtown to record while people borrowed his ideas
summary: He recorded only for himself with a portable tape recorder, was hurt that no one called him to record, and says Bird took ideas from him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, just for myself. Nobody ever called me to go downtown. Oh. Benny Green, may God rest his soul, he called me downtown. I did one thing with him which was called "Tenor Saxophone Shuffle," that was my song. But nobody actually really called me to come downtown. That's one thing that really hurt me, but it's all right, things are beginning to work out now.
You mean during the years that you were at the Paradise, you would have enjoyed going downtown on occasion, at least...

I would have loved to make some recordings, you know, everybody...you know, I wasn't makin' any recordins...I had the hottest spot in Harlem and everybody was comin' there and they were usin' my things and my ideas and goin' downtown and recording them. I couldn't even record. Nobody approached me, see? But that hurt, but I didn't say anything.
Yeah. You were aware that people
were doing that when people were there...

Well, Bird did it. Yeah, Bird. I don't know who else did it, but there was nothin' I could do about it, you know. I'm on stage and, you know, I was naked out there, you know, if they wanted to pick up somethin', they pick it up, you know. Yeah.
